long_biography.plain_text:
Neglected New York transit hubs were Andrew Zaro’s first proving ground. After college, he joined his family’s Bronx bakery business and expanded into Grand Central and other transport locations, helping Zaro’s Bread Basket grow into a substantial city chain. He sold his stake before moving into consumer credit.

A successful investment in non-performing loans drew Zaro into debt buying. He founded Cavalry Investments, where disciplined portfolio pricing and data-led collection decisions built a large private financial-services company. Outside finance, he has served on Columbia Grammar and Preparatory School’s board since 2005, later chairing it through expansions, leadership changes and economic downturns.

Forbes and Zaro's first-person statement date his move into his own financial-services platform to 1991, while the USC-sourced biography says the current Cavalry entity was formed in 1998 and refers to a predecessor. The biographies omit a founding year and preserve the durable sequence without forcing the entity dates to match.

Zaro's 2025 statement establishes that River Rock Holdings owns and operates multiple consumer- and real-estate-finance businesses, but it does not publish a complete portfolio, ownership percentages or valuations. Classifications therefore describe the verified sector and relationship without itemising or valuing private assets.

The family bakery supplied relevant operating experience and a stake Zaro later sold, and Forbes reports help from his real-estate-developer father-in-law when he opened his own shop. The form and value of that help are not disclosed, so it is recorded as an advantage rather than claimed as transferred ownership of Cavalry.
